title: Force Sensing in a Recoverable Bosonic Quantum Memory
authors: Tairong Bai, Wen Zheng, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Yangyang Ge, Kun Zhou, Xiangmin Yu, Yu Zhang, Shaoxiong Li, Xinsheng Tan, Jie Zhao, Yang Yu
abstract: In continuous-variable quantum information, sensing and quantum error correction in the same mode face an intrinsic trade-off: sensors must accumulate weak external displacements, whereas bosonic codes typically suppress such shifts as errors. Here, we establish compatibility by constructing finite-energy bosonic codes that enable a single oscillator to sense an external force while actively protecting an unknown logical qubit. By encoding logical amplitudes across discrete wave-packet sites and capturing the force signal in a shared internal coordinate, we achieve an endpoint probe readout that is independent of the logical state under continuous photon loss $γ$. Crucially, binomial site recovery cancels packet-dependent probe distortions alongside logical errors: for a $(2r+2)$-packet code, memory infidelity is suppressed to $O(γ^{r+1})$ while residual memory-probe correlations scale as $O(γ^{r+2})$. Finally, superconducting quantum circuit benchmarks under competing photon-number dephasing and Kerr nonlinearity identify preferred encoding regimes for hardware implementation.
summary: This paper presents a method to overcome the fundamental conflict between quantum sensing and error correction in bosonic quantum memories. By designing specific finite-energy bosonic codes and implementing a binomial site recovery protocol, the authors enable the memory to sense external forces while actively protecting the stored quantum information. This results in highly suppressed errors and state-independent readout, paving the way for practical quantum sensing devices.
main_problem: The paper addresses the intrinsic trade-off between quantum sensing (which requires accumulating external displacements) and quantum error correction (which suppresses such shifts) within a single bosonic quantum memory.
main_result: By employing finite-energy bosonic codes and binomial site recovery, the authors achieve a protocol where the force sensing readout is independent of the logical state, suppressing memory infidelity to $O(\gamma^{r+1})$ and memory-probe correlations to $O(\gamma^{r+2})$.
method: The analysis involves constructing and analyzing the joint output channel mapping the encoded memory state to the recovered logical register and the unmeasured probe, utilizing systematic site recovery operators.
model_or_system: The system is a bosonic quantum memory, modeled using superconducting cavities, where logical information is encoded across discrete wave-packet sites, and the external force signal is captured in a shared internal coordinate.
key_observables: Memory Infidelity ($1 - F_e$), Probe Quantum Fisher Information ($F_Q$), and Memory-Probe Correlations.
important_parameters: Photon loss rate ($\gamma$), code size (number of packets $2r+2$), and the ratio of coherence times ($T/T_\phi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the displacement remains within a positive decoding guard, and it treats state preparation and endpoint controls as ideal impulses.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the encoding scheme (logical amplitudes across sites and a shared coordinate) and the full protocol circuit, showing encoding, force accumulation, readout, and recovery steps.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the encoding scheme, derives the joint output channel, proves the error suppression scaling using binomial site recovery, and concludes with superconducting circuit benchmarks comparing different noise regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, scalable theoretical framework for integrating sensing and QEC in bosonic systems, directly relevant to superconducting circuit implementations of quantum memories.
